messages:
alex: quick heads-up — during last night's playback audit I spotted sampling skew between live traffic and the replay harness. KV cache hit rates are ~12% lower in the harness for the same trace slice.
maya: ouch. that would explain the ~30ms tail increase we saw in the nightly throughput run?
alex: yep. tail up by 25-40ms on p95/p99 for Llama-variant runs. overall qps similar.
chris: any obvious cause? anonymization step changed tokens? sampling slice mismatch?
alex: likely both. anonymization replaced user strings which shifts tokenization boundaries; also our sampler currently buckets by session length then does uniform sampling inside buckets — that interacts poorly with the prefix cache warm-up.
sam: can you paste the sampler query?
alex: sure — snippet from the harness sampling job: ```sql
-- select traces for playback
with sessions as (
  select trace_id, seq_len, rnd()
  from prod_traces
  where created_at > now() - interval '7 days'
), buckets as (
  select *, ntile(8) over (order by seq_len) as len_bucket
  from sessions
)
select trace_id
from buckets
where len_bucket in (3,4,5)
order by rnd
limit 10000;
```
maya: two quick things: 1) the `rnd()` in SQL is different than the deterministic seed we use in harness replay, 2) replacing tokens in anonymization can change prefix hits because caching keys are byte-level.
chris: especially for split-subword tokenizers — whitespace edits move subword boundaries. we should either anonymize with token-aware mapping or preserve token lengths.
alex: agreed. I'm proposing a 2-step fix: token-aware anonymizer + switch sampler to deterministic reservoir sampling with a seeded RNG so the same trace IDs are picked every run.
sam: for determinism, we should also pin kernel selection and batching policy in the harness config. last week a kernel switch (auto-select new fused layernorm) caused tiny nondeterminism between runs.
chris: do we have evidence that kernel change created nondet? I thought parity diffs were small.
alex: parity diffs jumped after the kernel change: token output mismatches at token index ~0.0003 fraction of tokens. that correlates with the fused layernorm using float32->mixed rounding in some paths.
maya: that fractional mismatch could cascade to cache keys and make warmups diverge.
chris: okay — plan: 1) re-run parity with kernel pinned to old fallback, 2) add token-aware anonymizer, 3) update sampler to seeded reservoir, 4) compare KV hit-rate deltas and p95/p99.
sam: I'll add a config flag in the harness: `force_kernel_override` and `seed=1935000001` so experiments are reproducible.
alex: thanks. infra-bot: kicked off a job for the pinned-kernel re-run?
infra-bot: job playback-audit/pinned-kernel-1935000001 started. ETA ~45m. Logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/playback-audit/1935000001
maya: also let's measure batch size distribution — harness uses a relaxed batching heuristic to hit qps which might produce fewer small batches vs prod. that changes KV reuse patterns.
chris: good call. add a histogram export for batch sizes and inter-token latencies.
alex: noted. I'll update the harness PR with anonymizer + sampler changes after we confirm pinned-kernel parity.
sam: if parity still differs after pinning, next suspect is RNG within CUDA kernels. we might need a deterministic mode compile flag.
maya: file a follow-up if we hit that. for now let's see job results. :eyes: 
alex: thanks all — will post results when infra job finishes.
infra-bot: job playback-audit/pinned-kernel-1935000001 completed. status: SUCCESS. artifacts: https://ci.redwood.ai/playback-audit/1935000001/artifacts
alex: initial diff: KV hit-rate delta reduced from 12% -> 2.1% when pinned. p99 tail reduced by ~18ms. small token mismatches still present (~0.00005).
chris: that suggests kernel switch explained most of it. remaining mismatch might be anonymizer tokenization edge cases.
maya: i'll prototype token-length-preserving anonymizer tonight.
sam: I'll open an RFC to add `harness.deterministic_mode=true` and document the kernel pinning knob.
alex: awesome. closing this incident for now, re-open if diffs fail after anonymizer changes. :thumbsup:
